title: Toward a KKL Theorem for any HDX
summary: The KKL Theorem, a seminal result in boolean function analysis, characterizes the structure of low-influence (non-expanding) functions on the hypercube. While recent years have seen breakthrough results across a variety of areas relying on analogs of the KKL Theorem beyond the cube (e.g., on product spaces, Grassmann graphs), further progress has been inhibited by our poor understanding of the phenomenon across more general domains.
